chunks: Those before you passed away because of the lengthening of their desires and the forgetting of their death, till that promised event befell them about which excuses are turned down, repentance is denied and punishment and retribution is inflicted.
ai.seo_question: Why did previous nations perish according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali attributes the destruction of previous nations to 'long hopes' (tawallud al-amil), a state where procrastination in repentance leads to spiritual complacency until death arrives unexpectedly. This concept highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing hope in mercy with the urgency of the 'hour of death' (saa'at al-mawt), where excuses are no longer accepted. The passage serves as a warning against delaying spiritual preparation, emphasizing that divine punishment descends when the appointed time (ajal) finally arrives.
